    def route_cost(route):
        if not route:
            return 0
        c = matrix[depot][route[0]] + matrix[route[-1]][depot]
        for i in range(len(route) - 1):
            c += matrix[route[i]][route[i + 1]]
        return c

    def feasible_append_load(load_a, load_b):
        return load_a + load_b <= capacity

    # 1) Clarke-Wright savings with deterministic sorting and capacity checks
    unassigned = set(customers_list)
    if not unassigned:
        return []

    # Ensure no repeated customer ids
    customers = list(unassigned)

    routes = [[c] for c in customers]
    loads = {i: demands[c] for i, c in enumerate(customers)}  # route index -> load
    node_to_route = {c: i for i, c in enumerate(customers)}

    # savings(i,j) = d(depot,i)+d(depot,j)-d(i,j)

    for a in range(n):
        i = customers[a]
        di = matrix[depot][i]
        for b in range(a + 1, n):
            j = customers[b]
            s = di + matrix[depot][j] - matrix[i][j]
            # Deterministic tie-break: larger saving first, then smaller (i,j)
            savings.append((s, i, j))
    savings.sort(key=lambda x: (-x[0], x[1], x[2]))

        if route and route[-1] == node:

        return -1

def solve_cvrp(instance):
    depot = instance["depot_index"]
    customers_list = instance["customer_ids"]
    n = len(customers_list)
    demands = instance["demands"]
    capacity = instance["capacity"]
    matrix = instance["distance_matrix"]
    # Build deterministic initial routes and then improve with savings + local repairs

    # Helpers
    def route_cost(route):
        if not route:
            return 0
        c = matrix[depot][route[0]] + matrix[route[-1]][depot]
        for i in range(len(route) - 1):
            c += matrix[route[i]][route[i + 1]]
        return c

    def feasible_append_load(load_a, load_b):
        return load_a + load_b <= capacity

    # 1) Clarke-Wright savings with deterministic sorting and capacity checks
    unassigned = set(customers_list)
    if not unassigned:
        return []

    # Ensure no repeated customer ids
    customers = list(unassigned)

    routes = [[c] for c in customers]
    loads = {i: demands[c] for i, c in enumerate(customers)}  # route index -> load
    node_to_route = {c: i for i, c in enumerate(customers)}

    # Prepare list of savings pairs (i<j) to keep determinism
    # savings(i,j) = d(depot,i)+d(depot,j)-d(i,j)
    savings = []
    # Avoid O(n^2) sorting blowups? n up to ~213, fine.
    for a in range(n):
        i = customers[a]
        di = matrix[depot][i]
        for b in range(a + 1, n):
            j = customers[b]
            s = di + matrix[depot][j] - matrix[i][j]
            # Deterministic tie-break: larger saving first, then smaller (i,j)
            savings.append((s, i, j))
    savings.sort(key=lambda x: (-x[0], x[1], x[2]))

    def is_end(route, node):
        # return 0 if start, 1 if end, -1 otherwise
        if route and route[0] == node:
            return 0
        if route and route[-1] == node:
            return 1
        return -1

    def merge_routes(ra, i_node, rb, j_node):
        # Only allow ra end == i_node and rb start == j_node for append merge
        # We keep routes directed to preserve interpretability.
        if ra == rb:
            return False
        rA = routes[ra]
        rB = routes[rb]
        if not rA or not rB:
            return False
        if rA[-1] != i_node:
            return False
        if rB[0] != j_node:
            return False
        if loads[ra] + loads[rb] > capacity:
            return False
        # Merge
        routes[ra] = rA + rB
        loads[ra] = loads[ra] + loads[rb]
        # Mark rb empty
        for node in routes[rb]:
            node_to_route[node] = ra
        routes[rb] = []
        loads[rb] = 0
